zh.q: 桌上是些什么？教材图10.4-1 与图10.4-2 甲 的接法差在哪？
zh.concl: 单刀双掷开关把电容器分别接到「电源」和「电阻」两个回路。教材图10.4-1 的电流表串在公共支路（充、放电都流过它），图10.4-2 甲 的传感器只在放电支路——本课两种摆法都画，第 5 步会对着看。
points: 单刀双掷开关有三个位置，不是两个：中间断开、倒向 1（充电）、倒向 2（放电）。
教材两张图的接法不同：图10.4-1 的电阻与电流表在公共支路，图10.4-2 甲 的电阻与传感器只在放电支路。
电流传感器与 R 串在同一条放电支路上，测的是同一个电流；中央零刻度毫安表以中位为零，指针能一正一反（没有传感器时也可用灵敏电流计）。

zh.q: 开关倒向 1，电流往哪走？指针往哪边打？
zh.concl: 充电电流流进上极板、极板电荷增加；u_C 越高剩下的电压差越小，电流越小；u_C 追上 U 后电流为零。即使断开电源，两极板上的电荷由于相互吸引仍然被保存在电容器中（教材 p.38）。
points: 充电电流的方向是「流进上极板」，台面上那支箭头必须指向上极板。
图10.4-1 接法下充电也经过 R，所以指针是慢慢回零的（τ = R·C = 1.55 s），但它不会反偏。
充满的判据是 u_C 追上 U，不是「充够时间」；充满以后 i = 0。

zh.q: 把开关倒向 2，指针往哪边偏？板间电场反了吗？
zh.concl: 放电电流与充电方向相反（同一只表指针反偏就是最直观的证据）。这一段两段共用同一个 τ = R·C，充电与放电曲线关于 u_C = U/2 镜像；板间电场方向始终由上极板指向下极板，放电时不变、只是变弱。
points: 放电电流与充电电流方向相反；同一只中央零刻度表指针反偏，是最直观的证据。
两段都经过 R，所以共用同一个 τ = R·C：u_充 + u_放 = 8.00 V，|i_放| − i_充 = 0.00 mA。
u_C 单调下降，但板间电场方向始终不变——不要把「电流反向」讲成「电场反向」。

zh.q: 不用万用表，怎么从一张 I-t 图读出电容器原来存了多少电荷？
zh.concl: i = dq/dt，所以 i-t 曲线下的面积就是流过的电荷量：q = q₀ + S。格子法是同一个积分的粗略版本（教材 p.39 问题 (2) 就是让学生用格子估）。
points: 面积的单位是「电流 × 时间」= 电荷，正好是 mC。
放电段曲线在轴下方，q 从 3.76 mC 往下掉：曲线剩下的那部分面积才是电容器里还剩的电荷。
教材网格：小格 0.4 s × 0.2 mA = 0.08 mC，45 格 = 3.60 mC，比精确值小 3.6 %。

zh.q: 教材问：要测绘充电时的 I-t 图像，应该怎样连接电路？
zh.concl: 要测充电电流，必须让充电回路里也有 R、并把表接在公共支路上——这正是教材 p.39 末尾那个问题的答案。两种接法的时间尺度差 16 倍（τ_chg / τ_dis = r / R = 0.0606）。
points: 教材 p.39 末尾问了这个问题，答案是：把 R 与传感器挪到公共支路（图10.4-1 那种接法）。
挪过去以后充电变慢（τ 从 0.09 s 变 1.55 s），充电曲线才画得出来。
两段共用同一个 τ 时，u_充 + u_放 = 8.00 V、|i_放| − i_充 = 0.00 mA。

zh.q: 把电荷量和对应的电压一对一对记下来画图，会看到什么？
zh.concl: q ∝ u_C，比值 q/u_C 是一个只由电容器本身决定的量——这就是电容的定义 C = q/u_C。教材 p.40 用「两只相同电容器并联 → 电荷量与电压各减半」得到同一结论，本课把它做成定量版。
points: 记 4–6 组就够画直线，不用记满全过程；每记一行，屏幕上的点就多一个。
q 是面积测出来的（剩余电荷 = 这一时刻之后曲线下的面积），不是拿铭牌 C 乘 u_C 算出来的。
q/mC = 0.47 × u/V，两个量的数字不重样，学生不会把两个量当成一个。

zh.q: 换一只小电容，斜率和面积会怎么变？只换电阻呢？
zh.concl: 面积 = C·U、斜率 = C：电容变了两者都变，电阻变了两者都不变。q/u_C 由电容器自己决定，与它怎么放电无关。
points: R 变 → 面积与斜率都不变，只是曲线矮而宽（τ 从 1.55 s 变 2.21 s）。
「充得多快」和「最后搬走多少电荷」是两件事。

zh.q: 铭牌写着 470 μF，为什么测出来不是 470？
zh.concl: ① 456 μF ≠ 470 μF 是元件容差（真值 454.19 μF，−3.4 %），不是测错：铭牌是标称值，电解电容允许 ±10 %，所以电容必须测。② 测量本身的误差另算：毫安表 0.1 mA 量化与采样（默认工况 < 1 %）、电流顶表时曲线被削平使面积一定偏小（相对 1.6 %）、数格子法偏小 3.6 %。
points: 铭牌是标称值，测出来的是实际值，差 3 % 属于容差——所以电容要测。
测量本身的误差有方向：量化让读数抖，超量程让面积一定偏小，数格子法也偏小。
同一个种子、同一组控件读数可重复（这是软件性质，不是误差分类的依据）。

zh.q: 考核：自己选 U、R、C，让这一段测得出的电容够大、峰值又不顶表
zh.concl: 没有新结论，只是把前八步的关系连起来用一遍：峰值 |i(0)| = U/R 决定「顶不顶表」，q/u_C 用来求电容，而 u_C 充满才让放电初始电流等于 U/R——三者都由同一段放电曲线上的读数给出。
points: 前提：拨到 2 之前先把开关合向 1 充满——否则放电初始电流很小，反推出来的 U 也小（第 ③ 条判你不成立）。
峰值 |i(0)| = U/R 不能超过传感器量程的三分之一：R 换小到 1.0 kΩ 以下、或 U 调到 12 V 又配小 R，就会顶表。
要过第 ② 条就把电容换大（470 → 1000 μF）：测得 C 就是 q/u_C，和铭牌一样是这只电容自己的比例。

en.q: What's on the bench? How do the circuits in textbook Fig. 10.4-1 and Fig. 10.4-2(a) differ?
en.concl: The single-pole double-throw switch connects the capacitor either to the "supply" loop or to the "resistor" loop. In textbook Fig. 10.4-1 the ammeter is in the shared branch (both charging and discharging pass through it); in Fig. 10.4-2(a) the sensor is only in the discharge branch. This lesson draws both layouts and compares them in step 5.
points: The single-pole double-throw switch has three positions, not two: open in the middle, to 1 (charge), to 2 (discharge).
The textbook's two figures are wired differently: in Fig. 10.4-1 the resistor and ammeter are in the shared branch; in Fig. 10.4-2(a) the resistor and sensor are only in the discharge branch.

The current sensor is in series with R in the same discharge branch and measures the same current; the center-zero milliammeter has its zero in the middle, so the needle can swing either way (a sensitive galvanometer works too without a sensor).

en.q: With the switch at 1, which way does current flow? Which way does the needle swing?
en.concl: Charging current flows into the top plate and the plate charge increases; the higher u_C, the smaller the remaining voltage difference and the smaller the current; once u_C catches up with U the current is zero. Even with the supply disconnected, the charges on the two plates attract each other and stay stored in the capacitor (textbook p.38).
points: The charging current "flows into the top plate", so the arrow on the bench must point to the top plate.
In the Fig. 10.4-1 circuit charging also passes through R, so the needle returns to zero slowly (τ = R·C = 1.55 s), but it never swings the other way.
The test for fully charged is u_C catching up with U, not "charged long enough"; once full, i = 0.

en.q: With the switch at 2, which way does the needle swing? Does the field between the plates reverse?
en.concl: The discharge current flows opposite to the charging current (the same meter's needle swinging the other way is the most direct evidence). Here both parts share τ = R·C, so the charging and discharging curves mirror each other about u_C = U/2; the field between the plates always points from top plate to bottom plate, unchanged during discharge, only weaker.
points: The discharge current is opposite to the charging current; the same center-zero meter's needle swinging the other way is the most direct evidence.
Both parts pass through R, so they share τ = R·C: u_chg + u_dis = 8.00 V, |i_dis| − i_chg = 0.00 mA.
u_C falls steadily, but the field between the plates never changes direction; don't describe "the current reverses" as "the field reverses".

en.q: Without a multimeter, how can an I-t graph tell us how much charge the capacitor held?
en.concl: i = dq/dt, so the area under the i-t curve is the charge that has flowed: q = q₀ + S. Counting squares is a rough version of the same integral (textbook p.39 question (2) asks students to estimate with squares).
points: The unit of area is "current × time" = charge, conveniently in mC.
In discharge the curve is below the axis and q falls from 3.76 mC: the area under the rest of the curve is the charge still left in the capacitor.
Textbook grid: each square 0.4 s × 0.2 mA = 0.08 mC, 45 squares = 3.60 mC, 3.6 % below the exact value.

en.q: The textbook asks: to plot the I-t graph during charging, how should the circuit be connected?
en.concl: To measure the charging current, R must also be in the charging loop and the meter in the shared branch; this is the answer to the question at the end of textbook p.39. The time scales of the two circuits differ by a factor of 16 (τ_chg / τ_dis = r / R = 0.0606).
points: The end of textbook p.39 asks this, and the answer is: move R and the sensor into the shared branch (the Fig. 10.4-1 layout).
Once moved, charging slows (τ from 0.09 s to 1.55 s), and only then can the charging curve be drawn.
When both parts share the same τ, u_chg + u_dis = 8.00 V and |i_dis| − i_chg = 0.00 mA.

en.q: If we record charge and the matching voltage in pairs and plot them, what do we see?
en.concl: q ∝ u_C, and the ratio q/u_C is a quantity set only by the capacitor itself; this is the definition of capacitance C = q/u_C. Textbook p.40 reaches the same conclusion with "two identical capacitors in parallel → charge and voltage both halve"; this lesson makes it quantitative.
points: 4–6 sets are enough to draw the line; no need to record the whole process. Each row recorded adds a point on screen.
q is measured from the area (remaining charge = area under the curve after this moment), not calculated by multiplying the rated C by u_C.
q/mC = 0.47 × u/V, so the two numbers never match and students won't confuse the two quantities.

en.q: With a smaller capacitor, how do the slope and area change? What if only the resistor changes?
en.concl: Area = C·U and slope = C: change the capacitor and both change, change the resistor and neither does. q/u_C is set by the capacitor itself, regardless of how it discharges.
points: C changes → area and slope both change (3.73 → 1.75 mC, 0.4700 → 0.2200).
R changes → neither area nor slope changes; the curve is just lower and wider (τ from 1.55 s to 2.21 s).
"How fast it charges" and "how much charge is finally moved" are two different things.

en.q: The label says 470 μF. Why isn't the measured value 470?
en.concl: ① 456 μF ≠ 470 μF is the component tolerance (true value 454.19 μF, −3.4 %), not a measurement mistake: the label is a nominal value and electrolytic capacitors allow ±10 %, so capacitance must be measured. ② Errors in the measurement itself are separate: the milliammeter's 0.1 mA quantization and sampling (< 1 % by default), clipping when the current pins the meter, which always makes the area too small (1.6 % relative), and counting squares, 3.6 % low.
points: The label is a nominal value and the measurement gives the actual value; a 3 % difference is tolerance, which is why capacitance is measured.
Measurement errors have directions: quantization makes readings jitter, overrange always makes the area too small, and counting squares is also low.
With the same seed and the same control readings, results repeat (a property of the software, not a basis for classifying errors).

en.q: Check: choose your own U, R and C so that this part measures a large enough capacitance without the peak pinning the meter
en.concl: No new conclusion, just using the relations of the first eight steps together: the peak |i(0)| = U/R decides "whether it pins the meter", q/u_C gives the capacitance, and only a full charge makes the initial discharge current equal U/R; all three come from readings on the same discharge curve.
points: Prerequisite: throw to 1 and charge fully before switching to 2; otherwise the initial discharge current is small, the inferred U is small, and criterion ③ fails.
The peak |i(0)| = U/R must not exceed a third of the sensor's range: R below 1.0 kΩ, or U at 12 V with a small R, will pin the meter.
To pass criterion ② use a larger capacitor (470 → 1000 μF): the measured C is q/u_C, the capacitor's own ratio just like its label.
